transcript:
Doctor: Hi auntie, apa khabar, what's wrong today?
Patient: Doctor ah, my anak this one, he got demam already three days lah. Last night very panas, almost 39 degree.
Doctor: I see. Got batuk or runny nose?
Patient: Got batuk berkahak, sikit-sikit. Runny nose also got, since yesterday lor.
Doctor: He still drink water and eat normal?
Patient: Eat very less, drink can lah. Pee also kurang.
Doctor: Any vomit or cirit-birit?
Patient: No no, just demam and batuk.
Doctor: Okay let me check. Temp now 38.5, throat a bit red, lungs clear. Looks like viral upper respiratory infection. I give paracetamol syrup, 5ml every 6 hours kalau demam. Banyak minum air. If demam more than 39 or anak become very lemah or sesak, must come back straight away or go A&E. Review in three days if not better.

note_json.chief_complaint: Anak demam 3/7 with batuk and rhinorrhoea

subjective.history_of_present_illness: Mother reports child has had fever for three days, with peak temperature near 39 °C overnight. Productive cough ("batuk berkahak") in small amounts. Rhinorrhoea since yesterday. Reduced appetite, oral intake of fluids maintained. Reduced urine output noted by mother. No vomiting, no diarrhoea.

objective.physical_exam: Throat mildly erythematous. Chest clear on auscultation.

assessment.problem: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection in a child
assessment.differential: Early lower respiratory tract infection if symptoms progress

plan.rationale: Avoid dehydration given reduced urine output

plan.action: Review in 3 days if not improving
Return immediately if T > 39 °C, lethargy, or respiratory distress

note_json.follow_up: Review in 3 days if not improving; return / A&E immediately if fever > 39 °C, lethargy, or respiratory distress.
